title: Sensitive Output Review & Corrective Action SLA (Template)
summary: Template SLA for how Redwood and its customers will handle reported instances of sensitive or potentially harmful model outputs (PII leaks, defamatory claims, regulated advice, high-risk financial instructions). Focuses on time-to-acknowledgement, investigation windows, classification thresholds, corrective actions, customer communications, and audit evidence obligations.
purpose: Provide a contractual exhibit customers can attach to agreements that defines expectations and measurable timelines when model-generated outputs raise material risk to the customer or third parties. Not intended to replace statutory breach notification but to clarify operational responsibilities for model-output-specific events.
scope: Applies to inference requests routed through Redwood-hosted and dedicated runtimes and to private deployments where the customer opts into Redwood-managed incident coordination. Covers: output containing sensitive personal data, plausible actionable instructions that could cause harm, falsified regulatory/financial statements, or content that materially risks customer reputation or regulatory non-compliance.
definitions: "Sensitive Output": any model response reasonably likely to include or reveal sensitive personal data (as defined by applicable law), to provide harmful operational instructions, or to present materially false or actionable claims about identifiable individuals or entities.
"Incident Window": the period from the first report of Sensitive Output to final remediation and customer closure confirmation.

"Corrective Action": the set of technical or operational steps taken to prevent recurrence for the same model variant and prompt pattern (e.g., prompt-blocking rules, model parameter rollback, blacklist patterns, dataset corrections, routing changes).
"Customer Escalation Lead": named contact at customer organization responsible for approving remediation steps and sign-off on closure.
sla_commitments: Acknowledgement: Redwood will acknowledge receipt of a customer report within 4 business hours for P1-level sensitive outputs and within 48 business hours for lower-priority reports.

Initial Triage: Redwood will complete an initial triage and classification within 24 hours for P1 reports, and within 72 hours for P2/P3 reports. Triage includes reproduction attempt and risk classification (PII leak, harmful instruction, reputational falsehood, other).

Investigation & Interim Mitigation: For P1 incidents, Redwood will propose and optionally deploy interim mitigations (routing away from the model variant, temporary model hold, prompt filters) within 72 hours unless customer declines immediate mitigation.

Root-Cause & Remediation Plan: Redwood will deliver a remediation plan (root cause summary, recommended corrective actions, expected timeline) within 10 business days of triage completion for P1/P2 incidents.

Remediation Implementation: Implementation timelines are mutually agreed; as a baseline Redwood will commit to implementing low-risk mitigations (rate limits, response filters, prompt templates) within 15 business days and more complex fixes (model retrain/weight rollback, quantization changes) subject to a separate change-control schedule.
Customer Notification: Redwood will provide status updates at least once per business day for P1 events until resolution, and weekly for P2/P3 until closure.
Closure & Postmortem: A written postmortem with timeline, root cause, and preventive actions will be delivered within 20 business days after remediation and validated closure.

Escrow & Evidence: Upon reasonable request, Redwood will provide reproducible logs, redacted transcript evidence, and configuration snapshots to support customer audits, subject to access controls and agreed redaction rules.
classification_guidelines: Suggested priority mapping (example): P1 = outputs with confirmed PII exposure, explicit safety-critical instruction, or regulatory compliance risk; P2 = probable PII or clearly false regulated claims; P3 = ambiguous outputs likely to confuse users or cause reputational harm. Guidance should be tailored per-customer: customers may supply prompt sets, sensitive-field matchers, and acceptance thresholds at onboarding.
review_workflow: 1) Customer files report (form + example queries/responses) to designated Redwood intake endpoint (URL placeholder). 2) Automated pre-check runs (KV/prefix cache match, similarity scoring against known incidents) and flags duplicates. 3) Human analyst reproduces the output and captures deterministic steps. 4) Analyst classifies, assigns priority, and recommends mitigations. 5) Customer reviews mitigation options and approves deployment or requests alternatives. 6) Redwood implements approved mitigations and validates via testing harness. 7) Closure and postmortem delivery.
escalation_matrix: Level 2 (Engineering): model-safety-eng@redwood.com — engaged within 24 hours for P1
Level 3 (Customer Success / Legal): cs-lead and legal-incident@redwood.com — contacted within 48 hours for P1 or any incident with potential contractual/regulatory exposure
corrective_action_examples: Prompt-level mitigation: canonical prompt templates, refusal triggers, token-level blocklists
Routing/Model variant mitigation: route traffic away from problematic model variant to a hardened variant
KV/prefix caching adjustments: scrub cached prefixes that cause unintended completions
Inference-time response filtering: regex/semantic checks to redact or replace PII or harmful instructions
Model rollback or weight freeze: temporary revert to previous version until code/model fix is complete
Training-data remediation: remove/annotate seed data that induces harmful behaviors (subject to change-control)
evidence_requirements: For auditability Redwood will capture and provide: reproducible request/response pairs (redacted where necessary), model variant and hash, inference configuration (temperature, max tokens, top_p), queue and routing metadata, timestamps, and relevant rollout flags. Sensitive fields will be redacted per agreed schema prior to export. Export requests must be made via secure evidence access workflow (see linked artifacts).
privacy_and_compliance_notes: This exhibit does not replace statutory data breach timelines. Where outputs involve personal data that meet breach thresholds under applicable law, statutory notification requirements take precedence. The party responsible for external regulatory notification will be identified during triage and will follow the primary contract's breach and notification clauses.
change_control_and_testing: Non-trivial mitigations (model retrain, new quantization, or dataset changes) will follow the standard change-control process: proposal, risk assessment, canary rollout, monitoring window with rollback triggers, and final release. Redwood recommends a customer-approved acceptance test suite (prompt set + expected outcomes) for validating mitigations before full rollout.
billing_and_service_credits: Mitigation work performed as part of initial triage and low-overhead fixes is included in standard support. Extended engineering remediation (retraining, dataset surgery) may be billable as professional services unless covered by an enterprise support add-on. Service credit terms for SLA failures to be negotiated in the main agreement.
open_questions_and_todos: - Confirm customer opt-in option for Redwood-managed evidence export. - Define exact redaction schema for PII across major regions (EU/US/APAC). - Template customer acceptance test suite to include at least 200 prompt/result pairs per high-risk workflow. - Align on billing carve-outs for third-party forensic services.
notes_for_sales_and_legal_review: This template intended to be attached as an exhibit to the DPA or Master Services Agreement. Sales should surface whether the customer requires: (a) guaranteed daily updates for P1 incidents, (b) local legal presence for regulatory notification, (c) expanded evidence retention window. Legal should verify interaction with data retention and DPA clauses.
